setup: Sit on the floor or a flat bench with your knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands on the surface slightly behind and outside your hips with fingers pointing forward for support.
Lean your torso back slightly and lift your feet a few inches off the floor, engaging your core to balance on your pelvis.
steps: Simultaneously extend your legs straight forward while leaning your torso back slightly, keeping your feet elevated above the floor.
Pull your knees back in toward your chest while flexing your torso slightly forward to meet them.
Squeeze your abdominal muscles at the peak contraction, then repeat the movement smoothly under control.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you extend your legs and lean back; exhale forcefully as you pull your knees toward your chest.
cues: Keep feet hovering off the floor
Crunch your ribs toward your pelvis

common_faults.fault: Relying purely on momentum without contracting the abdominals
common_faults.correction: Slow the tempo down and pause for a brief squeeze when the knees are drawn fully into the chest.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lower back during leg extension
common_faults.correction: Maintain pelvic control and do not lower the legs beyond the point where you can keep your core tightly braced.

precautions: Avoid letting the lower back arch excessively if you have a history of lumbar discomfort; limit leg extension range as needed.

name: Seated Knee Tuck
summary: A bodyweight core exercise performed by balancing on the glutes with hands supported behind, alternately extending the legs forward and flexing the knees and spine toward the chest.
